1	# Tiny Legend — technical architecture
2	
3	Owner: the `architect` seat. Binds the builder (P2). Refines PLAN.md §3; does not overturn it. Content numbers (speeds, HP, maps, sprites) come from `docs/DESIGN.md`; this document only fixes the *shape* they must fit. The real types are in `src/core/types.ts` and are the source of truth where this prose and the code disagree.
4	
5	Reading order for the builder: §2 (contract) → §3 (subsystems) → §8 (slices). Everything else is reference.
6	
7	## 1. Package layout and module map
8	
9	Package root = repository root, zero runtime dependencies (PLAN.md §1). Scripts expected in `package.json` (project-setup creates them; listed here so the builder knows the gates):
10	
11	| Script | Runs | Gate |
12	| --- | --- | --- |
13	| `dev` | `vite` | manual play |
14	| `build` | `tsc --noEmit && vite build` | must exit 0 |
15	| `preview` | `vite preview` | used by Playwright `webServer` |
16	| `test` | `vitest run` | unit + scripted playthrough |
17	| `test:e2e` | `playwright test` | browser smoke |
18	| `typecheck` | `tsc --noEmit` | strict + `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` |
19	
20	Dependency rule (enforced by `tests/purity.test.ts`, §5): `src/core/**` imports only from `src/core/**`. `src/content/**` imports only `src/core/types.ts`. `src/render/**` and `src/input/**` import core types and read state; they never mutate it. `src/main.ts` is the only file that wires everything together.
21	
22	### Module map
23	
24	Budgets are hard caps (PLAN.md §3.4: every `.ts` under 300). If a file is about to exceed its budget, split by concern — do not raise the budget.
25	
26	| File | Responsibility (one line) | Budget |
27	| --- | --- | ---: |
28	| `src/core/types.ts` | All shared types and the geometry constants. No logic, no imports. (Actual: 299.) | 299 |
29	| `src/core/rng.ts` | mulberry32: `nextU32(state)`, `randInt(state, n)`, `chance(state, percent)`, `pick(state, arr)`. | 40 |
30	| `src/core/geom.ts` | `rectOf(pos, box)`, `overlaps(a, b)`, `dirVec(dir)`, `opposite(dir)`, `dirToward(from, to)` (dominant axis), `clamp`. | 70 |
31	| `src/core/tilemap.ts` | Tile lookup by pixel/col/row, passability queries, `moveAxis()` — AABB vs. tile grid with snap-to-edge; treats out-of-bounds as solid. | 130 |
32	| `src/core/parse.ts` | `parseRoom(def, legend)` → `TileChar[]`, `validateContent(content)`. Throws with a precise message on any malformed data. | 110 |
33	| `src/core/state.ts` | `createState(content, seed)`, `newGame`, `enterRoom` (build tiles from def + progress, spawn enemies/items), `respawnAfterDeath`. | 140 |
34	| `src/core/step.ts` | `step(state, input)`: input swap, mode dispatch, the fixed per-frame order for `playing`, dead-entity sweep, `frame++`. `pressed(state, key)`. | 120 |
35	| `src/core/player.ts` | Movement from input, facing, edge-of-room detection (requests a transition), warp detection, sword swing, `hurtPlayer`, knockback tick. | 170 |
36	| `src/core/combat.ts` | `swordRect(state)`, sword vs. enemies, projectiles vs. player, enemies vs. player, `hitEnemy`, drop roll, boss-kill flag. | 140 |
37	| `src/core/enemies.ts` | `updateEnemies(state)`: one phase machine per behaviour (`shooter`, `flier`, `chaser`, `boss`) driven by `EnemyTiming`; enemy movement via `moveAxis`. | 220 |

39	| `src/core/items.ts` | `spawnPickup`, `applyPickup` (each `ItemKind`), `tryUnlockDoor`, `checkWarp`, `checkWin`. | 120 |

55	| **Sum `src/`** | | **3369** |
56	| `tests/helpers.ts` | `tinyContent` fixture (2×1 rooms, one enemy kind), `makeState(seed, content?)`, `runScript(state, steps)`, `holdFor(state, input, frames)`. | 120 |

58	| `tests/rng.test.ts` | Known mulberry32 sequence for a seed; `randInt` range. | 40 |

60	| `tests/player.test.ts` | Speed per frame, facing, wall stop, i-frames, knockback stops at walls. | 120 |
61	| `tests/transition.test.ts` | Edge exit starts a transition, entities frozen, placement on opposite edge, no neighbour = clamp. | 100 |
62	| `tests/combat.test.ts` | Sword hitbox per facing, damage, enemy knockback, drop roll under a fixed seed, i-frame immunity. | 140 |

65	| `tests/modes.test.ts` | Title → playing, pause toggle, game-over hold, win → title, death keeps progress. | 100 |
66	| `tests/purity.test.ts` | Greps `src/core/**` for `Math.random`, `Date`, `performance`, `window`, `document`, and non-core imports. | 40 |
67	| `tests/determinism.test.ts` | Same seed + same script twice → identical state; different seed → different RNG. | 60 |
68	| `tests/playthrough.test.ts` | Recorded input script from Title to Win under seed 1. | 150 |
69	| `e2e/smoke.spec.ts` | Page loads, canvas 256×240, `__game` present, non-black pixels > 0, right-arrow increases `player.x`. | 60 |

73	The `tests/**` and `e2e/**` files beyond `smoke` are created by the builder in the slice that needs them (§8). Project-setup creates `src/render/canvas.ts`, `src/main.ts`, `tests/smoke.test.ts` and `e2e/smoke.spec.ts` in P1c; the builder replaces their placeholder bodies in slice (a).
74	
75	## 2. Core simulation contract
76	
77	The core is a pure TypeScript module tree with one entry point:
78	
79	```ts
80	// src/core/step.ts
81	export function step(state: GameState, input: Input): void;
82	```
83

1	# Tiny Legend — game design document
2	
3	Owner: the `designer` seat. Binds the builder; refines, never overturns, [`PLAN.md`](PLAN.md) §2 (scope) and §3 (technical shape). Companion files (split out because the maps and sprites alone exceed 600 lines):
4	
5	- [`design/maps.md`](design/maps.md) — §8 world maps (all 20 screens as 16×11 ASCII) and §9 spawns, with a self-check script.
6	- [`design/sprites.md`](design/sprites.md) — §11 palette and every sprite as ASCII, with a self-check script.
7	
8	Conventions used everywhere: the game runs at a fixed 60 Hz; every duration is in **frames** (60 = 1 s). Distances are in **px** at the virtual 256×240 resolution. A tile is 16×16 px. The play area is 16×11 tiles = 256×176 px, drawn at canvas y = 64..239 under the 64-px HUD; **all entity positions in this document are play-area coordinates** (add 64 to y when drawing). Hit points of the player are counted in **half-hearts** (`hp`), enemies in **sword hits**. All randomness uses the seeded RNG in the state (`rng.int(lo, hi)` = integer in `[lo, hi]` inclusive; `rng.pct()` = integer in `[0, 99]`).
9	
10	## 1. Pitch
11	
12	A lone hero wakes in a meadow with nothing. In a cave on that same meadow lies a sword. North-east, past a forest full of Brutes and a rockfall, a dungeon door is set into the mountain; inside, six rooms, a key, a locked door, and Gnarl the Cave Wyrm, who guards the Sunstone — the Artifact. Pick it up and the land is saved. That is the whole game: get the sword, cross the overworld, find the key, unlock the door, beat the boss, take the Artifact. A hidden second cave holds a Heart Container for those who explore. Five to eight minutes for a first clear, one screen at a time, NES Zelda rules: enemies respawn when you re-enter a screen, hearts are precious, and the sword is the only weapon.
13	
14	## 2. Controls
15	
16	Keyboard only. Input is sampled once per frame into `{ up, down, left, right, sword, start }` (held booleans) plus `swordPressed`, `startPressed` (true only on the frame the key went down — edge-triggered). Key repeat from the OS is ignored.
17	
18	| Action | Keys | Playing | Paused | Title / GameOver / Win |
19	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
20	| Move up | `ArrowUp`, `W` | move / face up | — | — |
21	| Move down | `ArrowDown`, `S` | move / face down | — | — |
22	| Move left | `ArrowLeft`, `A` | move / face left | — | — |
23	| Move right | `ArrowRight`, `D` | move / face right | — | — |
24	| Sword | `Z`, `J` (pressed) | swing (needs `hasSword`) | — | — |
25	| Start | `Enter` (pressed) | pause | resume | advance (see §3) |
26	
27	- Opposite keys held together cancel (no movement on that axis). When one horizontal and one vertical key are held, **vertical wins**; there is no diagonal movement.
28	- The browser default for arrow keys, space and Enter is prevented so the page never scrolls.
29	- No mouse or touch input. No gamepad. (Out of scope, §13.)
30	
31	## 3. Game states and flow
32	
33	```
34	        Enter                 Enter                  hp = 0
35	Title ───────► Playing ◄──────────► Paused     Playing ─────► GameOver ──Enter (after 120 f)──► Title
36	   ▲                                                                                                │
37	   └──────────────── Enter (after 120 f) ─── Win ◄──── Artifact hold ends ──── Playing ◄────────────┘
38	```
39	
40	Every state renders the full 256×240 canvas. All text is white unless stated; `PRESS ENTER` prompts blink (visible 30 frames, hidden 30 frames). Text is drawn with the renderer's own 8-px font (§10.3).
41	
42	| State | Shows | Input accepted | Transition |
43	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
44	| **Title** | Black. `TINY LEGEND` centred at y=72. `player-down` sprite at (120,104). `PRESS ENTER` centred at y=168. If `progress` exists (a Game Over happened this session), a second line `CONTINUE` at y=184 instead of nothing. | `startPressed`, ignored during the first 15 frames of the state | → Playing. With no `progress`: a fresh `World` (seed from `Date.now()` in the adapter, passed into the core). With `progress`: new `World` with the progress fields restored (§3.1), player at the start position with 6 hp. |
45	| **Playing** | HUD (§10) + current screen + entities. | all | Enter → Paused. `hp` reaches 0 → death sequence (§4.8) → GameOver. Artifact hold ends → Win. |
46	| **Paused** | The frozen Playing frame, plus `PAUSED` centred at y=160 (play-area y=96). Nothing updates. | `startPressed`, ignored during the first 15 frames | → Playing (nothing in the world changed). |
47	| **GameOver** | Black. `GAME OVER` in `R` centred at y=104. After 120 frames: `PRESS ENTER` at y=168. | `startPressed`, only after 120 frames | → Title with `progress` set (§3.1). |
48	| **Win** | Black. `YOU FOUND THE SUNSTONE` centred at y=88; `THE LAND IS SAVED` at y=104; `artifact` sprite at (120,128). After 120 frames: `PRESS ENTER` at y=176. | `startPressed`, only after 120 frames | → Title with `progress` cleared (the next start is a fresh game). |
49	
50	Sub-states inside Playing (not separate top-level states; Enter is ignored while they run):
51	
52	| Sub-state | Duration | What happens |
53	| --- | --- | --- |
54	| **Scroll** (screen edge) | 32 frames | The old and new screens are drawn side by side and slide 8 px per frame (256/32 horizontally; 176/32 = 5.5 px per frame vertically). No entity updates. The player sprite is drawn at its arrival position on the new screen, moving with it. Enemies of the old screen are discarded on frame 0; the new screen's enemies spawn on frame 32. |
55	| **Warp** (`C`/`D`/`X`) | 20 frames | Play area black; HUD still drawn. On frame 20 the destination screen is loaded and its enemies spawn. |
56	| **Hold** (big item pickup) | 60 frames | §5.3. Nothing moves except the timer. |
57	| **Dying** | 60 frames | §4.8. |
58	
59	### 3.1 Progress kept across Game Over
60	
61	`progress = { hasSword, maxHp, rupees, keys, collectedItems, unlockedDoors, bossDefeated, visitedScreens }`. Restored on continue. Not kept: current hp (reset to 6), current screen and position (reset to start), live enemies, drops, the boss's current hp (it is either dead or full).
62	
63	## 4. Player
64	
65	### 4.1 Numbers
66	
67	| Property | Value |
68	| --- | --- |
69	| Sprite | 16×16, `player-<facing>` |
70	| Hitbox | 12×12 at offset (2,2) from the sprite's top-left |
71	| Position | `x, y` floats (px, play area); drawn at `Math.floor` |
72	| Speed | 1.5 px/frame while a direction is held and not blocked |
73	| Facings | up, down, left, right; changes to the held direction on any frame the player moves or tries to move (blocked movement still turns) |
74	| Start hp / max hp | 6 / 6 (3 hearts); max hp cap 10 (5 hearts) |
75	| Start position | screen `ow:1,2`, sprite at (112,112), facing up (maps.md §8.1) |
76	
77	### 4.2 Movement and tile collision
78	
79	Each frame, if not in Swing, Knockback, Hold or Dying: compute the intended delta (±1.5 on one axis). Move on that axis, then resolve against solid tiles: for every tile overlapped by the hitbox after the move, if the tile is solid (§7), push the hitbox back flush against that tile's edge and stop. Tiles outside the 16×11 grid are treated as **passable for the player** so that walking off the edge triggers a Scroll (§4.3). Conditional tiles: `L` is solid unless `keys > 0`, in which case touching it consumes a key (§5.2); `S` is solid while any enemy on the screen is alive; `C`, `D`, `X` are passable and trigger a Warp when the hitbox **centre** lies inside them.
80	
81	Optional polish (slice d, not required): NES-style corner nudge — when blocked while moving along an axis, if the hitbox overlaps the blocking tile by ≤ 4 px on the perpendicular axis, slide 1 px per frame on that axis away from the tile instead of stopping.

## 12. Difficulty and pacing

Expected first clear: **5–8 minutes**. Budget for a player who knows the route: sword cave 15 s, overworld to the dungeon 90 s including two fights, Heart Container detour 45 s, dungeon rooms 90 s, boss 30–45 s, walking and menus 30 s ≈ 5 min. A first-time player wanders ~2 extra minutes.

Where deaths are likely, in order:

1. **Deep Wood (ow:2,1)** — two Brutes at 2 damage each plus two Bats; the first real fight, with only 3 hearts. Mitigation: the Brutes start 9 tiles apart and Wander until the player is within 80 px, so one can be fought at a time by staying near the entry; Brutes drop a Heart 30 % of the time.
2. **Key Room (dg:0,0)** — two Brutes converge on the key. Mitigation: the key is on the far side from the door, but the pillars at (3,3), (12,3), (3,7), (12,7) let the player break line of pursuit; the Bat Cellar next door holds a guaranteed Heart.
3. **Gnarl** — §6.4. Mitigation: the telegraph, the guaranteed Heart from Bat Cellar and the Heart Container.

Octos and Bats are attrition, not killers: 1 damage each, 60 frames of invincibility per hit, and their drop tables give hearts back on average every 4–8 kills.

What makes it feel like the NES: enemies respawn so backtracking costs something; hearts cap at 5 so no grinding makes the boss trivial; the sword's reach (12 px) versus a Brute's 12×12 hitbox at 1.0 px/frame means hitting a chaser without trading is a timing skill, and the 20-frame Hurt knockback (16 px) is the reward.

Operator's request, verbatim: _"plan, build and test a small action RPG in the style of the NES Legend of Zelda."_ You own the **technical shape**: module structure, core types, the simulation contract, adapters, test seams and the build-slice plan a single builder will execute. 1	# Tiny Legend — game design document
2	
3	Owner: the `designer` seat. Binds the builder; refines, never overturns, [`PLAN.md`](PLAN.md) §2 (scope) and §3 (technical shape). Companion files (split out because the maps and sprites alone exceed 600 lines):
4	
5	- [`design/maps.md`](design/maps.md) — §8 world maps (all 20 screens as 16×11 ASCII) and §9 spawns, with a self-check script.
6	- [`design/sprites.md`](design/sprites.md) — §11 palette and every sprite as ASCII, with a self-check script.
7	
8	Conventions used everywhere: the game runs at a fixed 60 Hz; every duration is in **frames** (60 = 1 s). Distances are in **px** at the virtual 256×240 resolution. A tile is 16×16 px. The play area is 16×11 tiles = 256×176 px, drawn at canvas y = 64..239 under the 64-px HUD; **all entity positions in this document are play-area coordinates** (add 64 to y when drawing). Hit points of the player are counted in **half-hearts** (`hp`), enemies in **sword hits**. All randomness uses the seeded RNG in the state (`rng.int(lo, hi)` = integer in `[lo, hi]` inclusive; `rng.pct()` = integer in `[0, 99]`).
9	
10	## 1. Pitch
11	
12	A lone hero wakes in a meadow with nothing. In a cave on that same meadow lies a sword. North-east, past a forest full of Brutes and a rockfall, a dungeon door is set into the mountain; inside, six rooms, a key, a locked door, and Gnarl the Cave Wyrm, who guards the Sunstone — the Artifact. Pick it up and the land is saved. That is the whole game: get the sword, cross the overworld, find the key, unlock the door, beat the boss, take the Artifact. A hidden second cave holds a Heart Container for those who explore. Five to eight minutes for a first clear, one screen at a time, NES Zelda rules: enemies respawn when you re-enter a screen, hearts are precious, and the sword is the only weapon.
13	
14	## 2. Controls
15	
16	Keyboard only. Input is sampled once per frame into `{ up, down, left, right, sword, start }` (held booleans) plus `swordPressed`, `startPressed` (true only on the frame the key went down — edge-triggered). Key repeat from the OS is ignored.
17	
18	| Action | Keys | Playing | Paused | Title / GameOver / Win |
19	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
20	| Move up | `ArrowUp`, `W` | move / face up | — | — |
21	| Move down | `ArrowDown`, `S` | move / face down | — | — |
22	| Move left | `ArrowLeft`, `A` | move / face left | — | — |
23	| Move right | `ArrowRight`, `D` | move / face right | — | — |
24	| Sword | `Z`, `J` (pressed) | swing (needs `hasSword`) | — | — |
25	| Start | `Enter` (pressed) | pause | resume | advance (see §3) |
26	
27	- Opposite keys held together cancel (no movement on that axis). When one horizontal and one vertical key are held, **vertical wins**; there is no diagonal movement.
28	- The browser default for arrow keys, space and Enter is prevented so the page never scrolls.
29	- No mouse or touch input. No gamepad. (Out of scope, §13.)
30	
31	## 3. Game states and flow
32	
33	```
34	        Enter                 Enter                  hp = 0
35	Title ───────► Playing ◄──────────► Paused     Playing ─────► GameOver ──Enter (after 120 f)──► Title
36	   ▲                                                                                                │
37	   └──────────────── Enter (after 120 f) ─── Win ◄──── Artifact hold ends ──── Playing ◄────────────┘
38	```
39	
40	Every state renders the full 256×240 canvas. All text is white unless stated; `PRESS ENTER` prompts blink (visible 30 frames, hidden 30 frames). Text is drawn with the renderer's own 8-px font (§10.3).
41	
42	| State | Shows | Input accepted | Transition |
43	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
44	| **Title** | Black. `TINY LEGEND` centred at y=72. `player-down` sprite at (120,104). `PRESS ENTER` centred at y=168. If `progress` exists (a Game Over happened this session), a second line `CONTINUE` at y=184 instead of nothing. | `startPressed`, ignored during the first 15 frames of the state | → Playing. With no `progress`: a fresh `World` (seed from `Date.now()` in the adapter, passed into the core). With `progress`: new `World` with the progress fields restored (§3.1), player at the start position with 6 hp. |
45	| **Playing** | HUD (§10) + current screen + entities. | all | Enter → Paused. `hp` reaches 0 → death sequence (§4.8) → GameOver. Artifact hold ends → Win. |
46	| **Paused** | The frozen Playing frame, plus `PAUSED` centred at y=160 (play-area y=96). Nothing updates. | `startPressed`, ignored during the first 15 frames | → Playing (nothing in the world changed). |
47	| **GameOver** | Black. `GAME OVER` in `R` centred at y=104. After 120 frames: `PRESS ENTER` at y=168. | `startPressed`, only after 120 frames | → Title with `progress` set (§3.1). |
48	| **Win** | Black. `YOU FOUND THE SUNSTONE` centred at y=88; `THE LAND IS SAVED` at y=104; `artifact` sprite at (120,128). After 120 frames: `PRESS ENTER` at y=176. | `startPressed`, only after 120 frames | → Title with `progress` cleared (the next start is a fresh game). |
49	
50	Sub-states inside Playing (not separate top-level states; Enter is ignored while they run):
51	
52	| Sub-state | Duration | What happens |
53	| --- | --- | --- |
54	| **Scroll** (screen edge) | 32 frames | The old and new screens are drawn side by side and slide 8 px per frame (256/32 horizontally; 176/32 = 5.5 px per frame vertically). No entity updates. The player sprite is drawn at its arrival position on the new screen, moving with it. Enemies of the old screen are discarded on frame 0; the new screen's enemies spawn on frame 32. |
55	| **Warp** (`C`/`D`/`X`) | 20 frames | Play area black; HUD still drawn. On frame 20 the destination screen is loaded and its enemies spawn. |
56	| **Hold** (big item pickup) | 60 frames | §5.3. Nothing moves except the timer. |
57	| **Dying** | 60 frames | §4.8. |
58	
59	### 3.1 Progress kept across Game Over
60	
61	`progress = { hasSword, maxHp, rupees, keys, collectedItems, unlockedDoors, bossDefeated, visitedScreens }`. Restored on continue. Not kept: current hp (reset to 6), current screen and position (reset to start), live enemies, drops, the boss's current hp (it is either dead or full).
62	
63	## 4. Player
64	
65	### 4.1 Numbers
66	
67	| Property | Value |
68	| --- | --- |
69	| Sprite | 16×16, `player-<facing>` |
70	| Hitbox | 12×12 at offset (2,2) from the sprite's top-left |
71	| Position | `x, y` floats (px, play area); drawn at `Math.floor` |
72	| Speed | 1.5 px/frame while a direction is held and not blocked |
73	| Facings | up, down, left, right; changes to the held direction on any frame the player moves or tries to move (blocked movement still turns) |
74	| Start hp / max hp | 6 / 6 (3 hearts); max hp cap 10 (5 hearts) |
75	| Start position | screen `ow:1,2`, sprite at (112,112), facing up (maps.md §8.1) |
76	
77	### 4.2 Movement and tile collision
78	
79	Each frame, if not in Swing, Knockback, Hold or Dying: compute the intended delta (±1.5 on one axis). Move on that axis, then resolve against solid tiles: for every tile overlapped by the hitbox after the move, if the tile is solid (§7), push the hitbox back flush against that tile's edge and stop. Tiles outside the 16×11 grid are treated as **passable for the player** so that walking off the edge triggers a Scroll (§4.3). Conditional tiles: `L` is solid unless `keys > 0`, in which case touching it consumes a key (§5.2); `S` is solid while any enemy on the screen is alive; `C`, `D`, `X` are passable and trigger a Warp when the hitbox **centre** lies inside them.
80	
81	Optional polish (slice d, not required): NES-style corner nudge — when blocked while moving along an axis, if the hitbox overlaps the blocking tile by ≤ 4 px on the perpendicular axis, slide 1 px per frame on that axis away from the tile instead of stopping.
82

84

The play area is 16×11 tiles = 256×176 px, drawn at canvas y = 64..239 under the 64-px HUD; **all entity positions in this document are play-area coordinates** (add 64 to y when drawing). Hit points of the player are counted in **half-hearts** (`hp`), enemies in **sword hits**. All randomness uses the seeded RNG in the state (`rng.int(lo, hi)` = integer in `[lo, hi]` inclusive; `rng.pct()` = integer in `[0, 99]`).
9	
10	## 1. Pitch
11	
12	A lone hero wakes in a meadow with nothing. In a cave on that same meadow lies a sword. North-east, past a forest full of Brutes and a rockfall, a dungeon door is set into the mountain; inside, six rooms, a key, a locked door, and Gnarl the Cave Wyrm, who guards the Sunstone — the Artifact. Pick it up and the land is saved. That is the whole game: get the sword, cross the overworld, find the key, unlock the door, beat the boss, take the Artifact. A hidden second cave holds a Heart Container for those who explore. Five to eight minutes for a first clear, one screen at a time, NES Zelda rules: enemies respawn when you re-enter a screen, hearts are precious, and the sword is the only weapon.
13	
14	## 2. Controls
15	
16	Keyboard only. Input is sampled once per frame into `{ up, down, left, right, sword, start }` (held booleans) plus `swordPressed`, `startPressed` (true only on the frame the key went down — edge-triggered). Key repeat from the OS is ignored.
17	
18	| Action | Keys | Playing | Paused | Title / GameOver / Win |
19	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
20	| Move up | `ArrowUp`, `W` | move / face up | — | — |
21	| Move down | `ArrowDown`, `S` | move / face down | — | — |
22	| Move left | `ArrowLeft`, `A` | move / face left | — | — |
23	| Move right | `ArrowRight`, `D` | move / face right | — | — |
24	| Sword | `Z`, `J` (pressed) | swing (needs `hasSword`) | — | — |
25	| Start | `Enter` (pressed) | pause | resume | advance (see §3) |
26	
27	- Opposite keys held together cancel (no movement on that axis). When one horizontal and one vertical key are held, **vertical wins**; there is no diagonal movement.
28	- The browser default for arrow keys, space and Enter is prevented so the page never scrolls.
29	- No mouse or touch input. No gamepad. (Out of scope, §13.)
30	
31	## 3. Game states and flow
32	
33	```
34	        Enter                 Enter                  hp = 0
35	Title ───────► Playing ◄──────────► Paused     Playing ─────► GameOver ──Enter (after 120 f)──► Title
36	   ▲                                                                                                │
37	   └──────────────── Enter (after 120 f) ─── Win ◄──── Artifact hold ends ──── Playing ◄────────────┘
38	```
39	
40	Every state renders the full 256×240 canvas. All text is white unless stated; `PRESS ENTER` prompts blink (visible 30 frames, hidden 30 frames). Text is drawn with the renderer's own 8-px font (§10.3).
41	
42	| State | Shows | Input accepted | Transition |
43	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
44	| **Title** | Black. `TINY LEGEND` centred at y=72. `player-down` sprite at (120,104). `PRESS ENTER` centred at y=168. If `progress` exists (a Game Over happened this session), a second line `CONTINUE` at y=184 instead of nothing. | `startPressed`, ignored during the first 15 frames of the state | → Playing. With no `progress`: a fresh `World` (seed from `Date.now()` in the adapter, passed into the core). With `progress`: new `World` with the progress fields restored (§3.1), player at the start position with 6 hp. |
45	| **Playing** | HUD (§10) + current screen + entities. | all | Enter → Paused. `hp` reaches 0 → death sequence (§4.8) → GameOver. Artifact hold ends → Win. |
46	| **Paused** | The frozen Playing frame, plus `PAUSED` centred at y=160 (play-area y=96). Nothing updates. | `startPressed`, ignored during the first 15 frames | → Playing (nothing in the world changed). |
47	| **GameOver** | Black. `GAME OVER` in `R` centred at y=104. After 120 frames: `PRESS ENTER` at y=168. | `startPressed`, only after 120 frames | → Title with `progress` set (§3.1). |
48	| **Win** | Black. `YOU FOUND THE SUNSTONE` centred at y=88; `THE LAND IS SAVED` at y=104; `artifact` sprite at (120,128). After 120 frames: `PRESS ENTER` at y=176. | `startPressed`, only after 120 frames | → Title with `progress` cleared (the next start is a fresh game). |
49	
50	Sub-states inside Playing (not separate top-level states; Enter is ignored while they run):
51	
52	| Sub-state | Duration | What happens |
53	| --- | --- | --- |
54	| **Scroll** (screen edge) | 32 frames | The old and new screens are drawn side by side and slide 8 px per frame (256/32 horizontally; 176/32 = 5.5 px per frame vertically). No entity updates. The player sprite is drawn at its arrival position on the new screen, moving with it. Enemies of the old screen are discarded on frame 0; the new screen's enemies spawn on frame 32. |
55	| **Warp** (`C`/`D`/`X`) | 20 frames | Play area black; HUD still drawn. On frame 20 the destination screen is loaded and its enemies spawn. |
56	| **Hold** (big item pickup) | 60 frames | §5.3. Nothing moves except the timer. |
57	| **Dying** | 60 frames | §4.8. |
58	
59	### 3.1 Progress kept across Game Over
60	
61	`progress = { hasSword, maxHp, rupees, keys, collectedItems, unlockedDoors, bossDefeated, visitedScreens }`. Restored on continue. Not kept: current hp (reset to 6), current screen and position (reset to start), live enemies, drops, the boss's current hp (it is either dead or full).
62	
63	## 4. Player
64	
65	### 4.1 Numbers
66	
67	| Property | Value |
68	| --- | --- |
69	| Sprite | 16×16, `player-<facing>` |
70	| Hitbox | 12×12 at offset (2,2) from the sprite's top-left |
71	| Position | `x, y` floats (px, play area); drawn at `Math.floor` |
72	| Speed | 1.5 px/frame while a direction is held and not blocked |
73	| Facings | up, down, left, right; changes to the held direction on any frame the player moves or tries to move (blocked movement still turns) |
74	| Start hp / max hp | 6 / 6 (3 hearts); max hp cap 10 (5 hearts) |
75	| Start position | screen `ow:1,2`, sprite at (112,112), facing up (maps.md §8.1) |
76	
77	### 4.2 Movement and tile collision
78	
79	Each frame, if not in Swing, Knockback, Hold or Dying: compute the intended delta (±1.5 on one axis). Move on that axis, then resolve against solid tiles: for every tile overlapped by the hitbox after the move, if the tile is solid (§7), push the hitbox back flush against that tile's edge and stop. Tiles outside the 16×11 grid are treated as **passable for the player** so that walking off the edge triggers a Scroll (§4.3). Conditional tiles: `L` is solid unless `keys > 0`, in which case touching it consumes a key (§5.2); `S` is solid while any enemy on the screen is alive; `C`, `D`, `X` are passable and trigger a Warp when the hitbox **centre** lies inside them.
80	
81	Optional polish (slice d, not required): NES-style corner nudge — when blocked while moving along an axis, if the hitbox overlaps the blocking tile by ≤ 4 px on the perpendicular axis, slide 1 px per frame on that axis away from the tile instead of stopping.
82

1	# Brief — designer, P1a: game design document for "Tiny Legend"
2	
3	From: lead (pubkey `62e0374f…9639`). Assignment: `b7b201999f5ab5b077cf1cd152440f2dc3a9a03e8f7d19e4f9ef29ea49d4bbca` (kind 44244 — cite it as `assignmentRef` in your report).
4	
5	## The goal you serve
6	
7	Operator's request, verbatim: _"plan, build and test a small action RPG in the style of the NES Legend of Zelda."_ You own the **content design**: what the world is, what's in it, and how it behaves — written precisely enough that a builder who has never talked to you can implement it from the document alone.
8	
9	## Read first
10	
11	1. Your worktree is a checkout of the `rpg-test` repository (the game is the whole repo). Run `git merge nes-rpg-plan-lead` in your worktree to receive the lead's plan (branch head `64c9e9c6396f68491b41edb7c007018496a257a5`, based on `main` @ `340a064`), then read `docs/PLAN.md` — §2 (scope) and §3 (technical shape) bind you.
12	2. Two other seats work in parallel: an architect (`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, `src/core/types.ts`) and project-setup (package scaffold). You do not depend on them and they do not depend on you. Your files: `docs/DESIGN.md` (split into `docs/design/*.md` only if a single file passes ~600 lines). **Nothing else.**
13	
14	## Deliverable
15	
16	`docs/DESIGN.md`. Contents, in this order:
17	
18	1. **One-paragraph pitch** and the fantasy (lone hero, retrieve the Artifact from the dungeon).
19	2. **Controls** — exact key mapping (arrows + WASD move; `Z`/`J` sword; `Enter` start/pause), what each does in each game state.
20	3. **Game states & flow** — Title → Playing ⇄ Paused → GameOver → Title; Playing → Win → Title. What each screen shows, what input advances it, timings (e.g. game-over hold 2 s before accepting input).
21	4. **Player** — speed in px/frame at 60 Hz, hitbox in px (NES Link is a 16×16 sprite with a ~12×12 body box — pick and state), 4 facings, sword hitbox size/offset per facing and active frames, damage taken (1 heart or ½ heart per source), knockback distance/frames, invincibility frames, death.
22	5. **Hearts & items** — start 3 hearts, cap 5. Table of every item: Sword, Small Key, Heart (pickup, heals 1), Heart Container (+1 max, fills), Rupee (counter only, cap 255), Artifact (win). For each: where it appears, pickup rule, HUD effect.
23	6. **Enemies** — exactly three overworld/dungeon types + one boss, each with: name, HP, damage dealt, speed, hitbox, behaviour as a state machine (states, transitions, timers in frames), projectile stats if any, drop table (percent heart / rupee / nothing), which rooms they appear in. Suggested archetypes: wanderer-that-stops-and-shoots (Octorok-like), erratic flier (Keese-like), 2-HP chaser (Moblin-like), boss with 6 HP that spits projectiles in a pattern. Boss must be beatable with the basic sword by a careful player in under ~60 s.
24	7. **Tile legend** — one ASCII character per tile type, with: passable?, blocks projectiles?, visual (a name; the palette is yours), special behaviour (door, locked door, stairs/cave entrance, water, etc.). Keep it under ~12 tile types.
25	8. **World maps** — every screen as a 16-wide × 11-high ASCII block using the legend. Overworld: 4 columns × 3 rows = 12 screens, coordinates `(col,row)` with the start position stated; screens connect by edges (walking off the edge scrolls to the neighbour) so edge tiles must line up. Include: start screen with a cave entrance holding the Sword; a hidden Heart Container; the dungeon entrance. Dungeon: 6 rooms — entrance, two combat rooms, key room, locked door leading to boss room, treasure room with the Artifact — same 16×11 format, with door positions and which are locked. Provide a small overview grid for each map showing how rooms connect.
26	9. **Spawns** — per screen: enemies (type, tile position) and items (type, tile position). Spawn rule (respawn on re-entry? NES respawns; state whether the boss stays dead — it must).
27	10. **HUD** — 64px-tall strip: heart row, rupee counter, key counter, mini-map optional. Positions in px.
28	11. **Palette** — ≤ 16 named colours as hex, NES-flavoured. Sprites will be drawn programmatically from text, so also give an **8×8 or 16×16 ASCII sprite** for: player (one facing is enough; others may mirror), each enemy, sword, heart, rupee, key, artifact. Use one character per palette index, `.` for transparent.
29	12. **Difficulty & pacing** — expected time to win (~5–8 min), where the player is likely to die, what makes the boss fair.
30	13. **Out of scope** — list what you deliberately left out and why (keeps the builder from guessing).
31	
32	## Constraints
33	
34	- Every quantity is a number (frames, px, HP). "Fast" and "a bit" are defects.
35	- Everything must be representable as data: ASCII maps, tables. No behaviour that needs bespoke scripting beyond the enemy state machines you describe.
36	- Stay inside PLAN.md §2. If you believe a scope item is wrong for the game, say so in a "Proposed scope changes" appendix — do not silently design around it.
37	- Write only `docs/DESIGN.md` (or `docs/design/*.md`). Do not create code files. Do not edit `docs/PLAN.md`.

# Tiny Legend

A small action RPG in the style of the NES Legend of Zelda, running in the browser on a 256×240 canvas with no runtime dependencies.

## Run

```sh
pnpm install
pnpm dev        # http://localhost:5173
```

`pnpm build` type-checks and writes a production bundle to `dist/`; `pnpm preview` serves it on port 4173.

## Test

```sh
pnpm typecheck  # tsc --noEmit
pnpm test       # Vitest unit tests (tests/**/*.test.ts)
pnpm test:e2e   # Playwright browser smoke (e2e/**), builds and serves the bundle itself
```

Playwright uses the Chromium build already cached on this host; do not run `playwright install`.

## Docs

- [docs/PLAN.md](docs/PLAN.md) — scope, phases, test strategy, decisions (lead).
- [docs/DESIGN.md](docs/DESIGN.md) — maps, enemies, items, HUD, controls, sprites (designer).
- [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) — module map, core types, step contract (architect).

## Play

Arrows/WASD move, `Z`/`J` swing the sword, `Enter` starts, pauses and continues. Get the sword from the cave on the first screen, cross the overworld to the dungeon in the north-east, find the key, unlock the door, beat Gnarl and take the Sunstone.

`window.__game` is a debug handle (`state`, `step(input)`, `setInput`, `loadRoom`, `pause`, `reset(seed)`, `record`).

## Layout

- `src/main.ts` — entry point; fixed 60 Hz loop, keyboard, renderer, `window.__game`.
- `src/core/` — headless, deterministic simulation (`step(state, input)`); no DOM.
- `src/content/` — maps, sprites, stats and the tile legend as data (generated from `docs/design/*.md`).
- `src/input/`, `src/render/` — keyboard and canvas adapters.
- `tests/` — Vitest unit tests, including the recorded Title→Win playthrough (`tests/scripts/playthrough.ts`).
- `e2e/` — Playwright specs: smoke and a browser replay of the playthrough.
- `tools/playthrough.record.ts` — the bot that records the playthrough script (`pnpm exec vitest run --config tools/vitest.record.config.ts`).
